title: Stored heat (radiant and conduction time series) from Archie's own heat balance
basis: ASHRAE Handbook—Fundamentals 2009 Ch 18 Radiant Time Series method, with the time series calculated by Archie's own periodic heat balance (ai/stored_heat.py) from AIRAH Technical Handbook 2007 material properties, because ASHRAE's published RTS and CTS tables (Ch 18 Tables 16, 19 and 20) aren't available to us. Checked against ASHRAE's PRF/RTF generator results for two constructions (Journal of Engineering, Univ. of Baghdad, vol 21 no 5, 2015, Table 4) and ASHRAE 2009 Table 19 heavyweight / no carpet / 10% glass nonsolar series (reproduced in the same paper, Table 7).

sources.airah_2007: AIRAH Technical Handbook, 4th edition (2007); page numbers are the printed page numbers.
sources.nigusse_2007: Nigusse (2007), recommended radiative/convective splits adopted by ASHRAE Handbook—Fundamentals 2009 Ch 18, reproduced in Journal of Engineering (Univ. of Baghdad) vol 21 no 5 (2015) Table 1.
sources.ashrae_2009_zone: ASHRAE Handbook—Fundamentals 2009 Ch 18 Table 21 representative zone furnishings, 25 mm wood over 50% of the floor area; this is the reading that reproduced Table 19's heavyweight series (tests/test_stored_heat.py), not a value checked against Table 21 itself.

films.source: AIRAH 2007 p.150 Thermal resistance of air films (still air, high-emittance surface; 3 m/s summer outside); emittance p.151 (paint, any colour, 0.90-0.96; lower end).

clay_brick.source: AIRAH 2007 p.164, generic extruded brickwork 110 mm

dense_hollow_block.source: AIRAH 2007 p.166, dense-weight hollow concrete block

timber.source: AIRAH 2007 p.174, pine (weatherboards); the only timber row with a specific heat

wall_cavity.source: AIRAH 2007 p.151, vertical airspace, high emittance, 100 mm

ceiling_cavity.source: AIRAH 2007 p.151, horizontal airspace, heat flow down, high emittance, 100 mm

roof_space.source: AIRAH 2007 p.150, ventilated pitched roof space, summer, high emittance

carpet_and_underlay.source: AIRAH 2007 p.164, carpet 6 mm R0.058 + underlay 15 mm R0.24 (lower end of 0.24-0.41)

inside_film_vertical.source: AIRAH 2007 p.150, still air, vertical (the far face of a wall to an unconditioned space)

inside_film_down.source: AIRAH 2007 p.150, still air, heat flow down (the top face of a ceiling to a roof space)

wall_lightweight.label: lightweight framed wall (plasterboard, insulation, fibre-cement cladding)

wall_brick_veneer.label: brick veneer (plasterboard, insulation, cavity, 110 mm brick)

wall_cavity_brick.label: cavity brick (110 mm brick, insulated cavity, 110 mm brick)

wall_concrete.label: 150 mm concrete panel, insulated and plasterboard lined

wall_block.label: 190 mm concrete block, insulated and plasterboard lined

roof_metal.label: metal roof over a ventilated roof space, insulated plasterboard ceiling

roof_tile.label: clay-tile roof over a ventilated roof space, insulated plasterboard ceiling

roof_concrete.label: 150 mm concrete roof slab, insulated, plasterboard ceiling below

floor_timber_suspended.label: timber floor over a ventilated subfloor

floor_concrete_intermediate.label: 150 mm concrete floor with a suspended ceiling below

floor_timber_intermediate.label: timber upper floor on joists, plasterboard ceiling below

ceiling_suspended_under_slab.label: suspended acoustic-tile ceiling under a 150 mm concrete floor

ceiling_plasterboard_under_timber.label: plasterboard ceiling under a timber floor

ceiling_to_roof_space.label: insulated plasterboard ceiling under an unconditioned roof space

furnishings.label: furnishings: 25 mm timber over half the floor area, one face exposed

floor_coverings.basis: Carpet in house bedrooms and living rooms and in offices; a hard floor (tiles) everywhere else, including shops, kitchens, dining, wet areas and garages. A typical finish by room use; the drawings don't say.

defaults.basis: When the drawings don't name a construction: the lightest typical construction (a framed wall, a metal roof, plasterboard partitions), which takes the least credit for stored heat; a ground floor is a concrete slab on ground (the Phase 1 floor rule already takes a ground floor as a slab); a floor or ceiling between storeys is concrete with a suspended ceiling in a commercial building and timber with plasterboard in a house.

people.note: occupants, typical office conditions; sensible part only (latent heat reaches the air at once)

lighting.note: recessed fluorescent luminaire with lens, lower end of 0.40-0.50 (the split table gives no LED value); the lower end takes the least credit

equipment.note: no radiant split is applied to equipment until ASHRAE's equipment splits (2009 Ch 18 Tables 6-12) are available; all equipment heat reaches the air in its own hour, which takes no stored-heat credit

window_solar_unshaded.note: solar heat gain without interior shading, released by the solar time series

window_solar_inside_shade.note: with blinds or shades the split table says it varies and its source tables aren't available; taken as reaching the air at once, which takes no stored-heat credit
